summary: Ngawang Jorden works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

Ngawang Samten studied under traditional teachers Lati Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Tsering, Jampa Yeshe, and Konchok Tsering. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he was Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held positions at Smith College, Hampshire, Amherst, and the University of Tasmania.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at Punjabi University, attested in 2012, under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, and studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann, attested in 2013.

Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre, attested in 2009.
Nguyen Van Thuong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi, where K. T. S. Sarao served as his MA supervisor.

Nianzu Huang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology and with teachers including Lianju Xia, Gongga Rinpoche, Nordan Hutuktu, Hsu Yun, and Jiaqi Wang. He headed Central People's Broadcasting Station and was a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1955–1980).
Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) studied at Rissho University and worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded Nipponzan Myohoji.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama (1920–2001) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1976) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1976–1985).

Nicholas J. Allen (1939–2020) studied at Rugby School and the University of Oxford. A specialist in Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at SOAS, Durham University, and the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (~1976–2001).

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) studied at Saint Petersburg State University. Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, he held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the University of Washington.

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1893–1898) and the Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts (~1893–1897).
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University by 2015 and held a research fellow post at the University of Tokyo, attested in 2017.
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Indiana State University and Indiana University, and held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, the University of Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
Nicolas Morrissey studied under Gregory Schopen. Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, he holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University and under Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, and U-tain Wongsathit, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

Nicolas Tournadre, a linguist and Tibetologist, studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University and Paris 8 University. He held academic posts at INALCO, Paris 8, the University of Virginia, University of Provence - Aix-Marseille I, Aix-Marseille University, and LACITO.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She held positions at the École du Louvre (~1953–1976), the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1957–1971), and INALCO (~1971–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) studied at Østre Borgerdyd school and the universities of Copenhagen, Bonn, Paris, London, and Oxford. Specializing in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he became Professor für Indisch-orientalische Philologie at the University of Copenhagen in 1845.
